lectus, lectī m.

noun, second declension

bed or couch

Other words

  • torus, torī m. — a couch, a bed; properly its cushion or mattress

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.2 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 8.193: antīquīs torus ē strāmentō erat (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.)

Examples

  • Necesse est tibi manēre in lectō duōs trēsve diēs.

    You must stay in bed for two or three days.Traupman 56

  • lectō tenērī

    to be confined to bedCic. Verr. 2.5.16 (Lewis & Short s.v. lectus)

  • concutiuntque torum dē mollī flūminis ulvā impositum lectō spondā pedibusque salignīs

    and they shake up the mattress of soft river sedge, laid on a couch with frame and feet of willowOv. Met. 8.655–656

See also pillow, blanket, sheet, mattress, bed frame, make the bed, family bed, get up, go to bed, duvet.
